topic.topic: Why Gyms Make More Money When You Stay Home

claims.text: At December 31, 2025 Planet Fitness had approximately 20.8 million members and 2,896 clubs (2,604 franchised, 292 corporate-owned); a year earlier, 19.7 million members and 2,722 clubs.
The FY2025 10-K says members completed more than 650 million workouts in the company's clubs.
The 10-K describes its clubs as typically 20,000 square feet.
Classic Card dues start at $15 a month for new members and the PF Black Card at $24.99; the standard annual fee is $49; Black Card penetration was 66.5% at year-end 2025.
Over 90% of both corporate-owned club and franchise revenues were recurring: royalties, monthly dues and annual fees.
In a study of 7,752 members at three health clubs, members on a flat monthly fee of over $70 attended on average 4.3 times a month, paying over $17 per expected visit versus $10 on a 10-visit pass.
The Classic Card cost $10 a month from 1998 until the May 2024 announcement that new members would pay $15; existing members kept their $10 rate.
The FY2025 10-K says clubs open more than 12 months had average unit volumes of approximately $2.0 million.
The 10-K puts Planet Fitness's average franchise royalty rate at 6.7% (63% of clubs at the current rate), and franchisees contribute approximately 2% of dues to national advertising funds.
Franchisees must buy equipment from Planet Fitness (or required vendors in some international markets) and generally replace it every five to nine years, based on club volume.

The 10-K says that because clubs are typically 20,000 square feet and omit amenities such as group exercise classes and pools, there is more space for equipment members use, and the company has not needed time limits on cardio machines.
The 10-K says members may cancel at any time after giving proper notification, and for certain memberships subject to an initial minimum term.
